    How it works.

    Notion for company context, Snowflake as the governed data foundation.

    Data agents in action.

    Build with enterprise confidence.

    Grounded in your business

    Use the metric definitions, table context, company knowledge, and query guardrails set by your teams.

    Respects permissions

    Admins control who uses the agent. Users sign in with their own Snowflake credentials, so existing permissions apply.

    Sources you can check

    Review the data, definitions, and company context behind an answer before taking action on it.

    Workspace admins can monitor agent usage and Notion credit consumption. Every agent run is logged with full audit trails showing what triggered it, what it did, and why.

    FAQs

    How does a data agent work with Snowflake and Notion?

    A data agent brings together governed Snowflake data, relevant company knowledge, and clear instructions. When someone asks a question, it uses approved definitions and source guidance to investigate, then returns an answer with supporting sources. Data access is limited by the user’s Snowflake role and permissions.

    Notion gives teams a place to ask questions, review results, and put them to use in their work.

    For more detail, read How we built a personal data scientist for every Notion employee.

    How are permissions & access governed?

    A data agent can be implemented either as Custom Agent connected to Snowflake MCP, or invoked as a skill in Notion Agent. In both instances, each user is required to connect to Snowflake using their own credentials. Notion controls workspace access and available connections, while Snowflake enforces the approved role and data permissions for the person that's asking the question.

    Your data team defines the metrics, sources, filters, and query guardrails. If the data agent runs into missing definitions, failed checks, or if the user has insufficient Snowflake access, the agent surfaces those details instead of guessing the answer.

    How can I learn more about building a data agent?

    For a look at how we built our data agent with Notion AI and Snowflake, read How we built a personal data scientist for every Notion employee. If you’d like help building one for your team, request early access.

    Who is the Early Access program for?

    This is a guided program for teams with a recurring business question, trusted Snowflake data, and the people and time to build and test a first workflow together. A strong fit has a business champion, Notion and Snowflake owners, a data owner, a small committed pilot group, and a path through security review. Teams evaluating either platform can still express interest, and our team will review readiness and fit.

    What happens after I request access?

    Our team will review your use case and readiness. If accepted, we’ll guide your team through discovery, setup, and validation of one initial workflow. Because spots are limited, some qualified teams may be waitlisted.
